name: Coral bleaching
summary: NOAA has not declared a fifth global bleaching event as of 27 Nov; El Niño keeps the risk of one elevated
state: NOAA Coral Reef Watch says the fourth global bleaching event, which hit about 84% of reef area, likely ended in 2025, and its status page, last updated on 2 Jun 2026, declares no fifth event (NOAA). NOAA warned in June that El Niño could trigger a fifth global event (CBS News). Searches on 27 Nov found no new NOAA global declaration, so Normal holds, with risk rising as El Niño persists into the southern summer.
for_you: Bleaching risk is highest in the southern-hemisphere summer, including the Great Barrier Reef. Reef tourism and fisheries communities are most exposed if a new event is declared.
rubric_hit: Normal: NOAA has declared no global bleaching event in progress as of 27 Nov

sources.title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch — Current global bleaching: status update
CBS News — El Niño could bring more widespread coral bleaching, NOAA warns

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
